title: Matched-Receiver ManySig Random Forest Baseline
research_question: Can the existing 16-feature Random Forest distinguish the six ManySig transmitters when training and testing are restricted to a matched receiver condition?

dataset_provenance.sample_rate_status: REQUIRES VALIDATION (Engineering default inherited from Track-A)

model_configuration.provenance: Track-A D5 classical RF baseline specification

primary_temporal_holdout.name: Date-Holdout Protocol (Days 1-3 Train -> Day 4 Test)
primary_temporal_holdout.leakage_safeguard: Strict temporal date holdout. Test date 2021_03_23 is completely unseen during training.

secondary_matched_date_chunk_holdout.name: Burst-Block Holdout Protocol (70% Train, 15% Val, 15% Test within each leaf)
secondary_matched_date_chunk_holdout.leakage_safeguard: Contiguous block separation prevents burst-to-burst autocorrelation while testing matched-date performance.

tertiary_two_date_temporal_holdout.name: Two-Date Train Protocol (Days 1-2 Train -> Day 3 Val -> Day 4 Test)
tertiary_two_date_temporal_holdout.leakage_safeguard: Unseen validation and test dates to quantify temporal drift under limited training observation.

leakage_controls: Strict prohibition of uniform random row splitting (DEC-035)
Metadata columns (rx_id, capture_date, is_equalized, leaf_index, burst_index, sample_count) strictly excluded from input features
Model trained strictly on features from training partition
No hyperparameter tuning against test partitions
Closed-set 6-transmitter classification in controlled matched-receiver condition
